nodes.name: Electrodeposition of NiCr alloy
nodes.procedure: A constant current method was employed to deposit NiCr alloy onto Ni foam (denoted as NiCr@NF).
nodes.source_text: Figure S1 schematically illustrates the electrodeposition-sulfidization synthetic approach.32 Briefly, a constant current method was employed to deposit NiCr alloy onto Ni foam (denoted as NiCr@NF, Figure S2)

nodes.characterization_summary: Spherically shaped Ni₃S₂/Cr₂S₃ NPs sized 15-30 nm; SAED shows (110) plane of Ni₃S₂ and (113),(021) planes of Cr₂S₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the spherically shaped Ni₃S₂/Cr₂S₃ NPs sized from 15 to 30 nm can be depicted from the transmission electron microscopic (TEM) images (Figure 1b and S6), while the bright rings displayed in the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern (inset of Figure 1b) confirm the presence of the (110) plane of Ni₃S₂ and (113) and (021) planes of Cr₂S₃ crystals.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni, Cr, S elemental mapping shows Ni and Cr surrounded by each other in different NPs; composition 41.8 wt% Ni, 34.7 wt% Cr, 23.7 wt% S.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The aberration-corrected scanning transmission electron microscopic (STEM) image and the corresponding EDX elemental mapping images (Figure 1c) clearly elucidate that Ni and Cr are surrounded by each other... Ni, Cr, and S contents derived from the STEM-EDX spectrum of Ni₃S₂/Cr₂S₃@NF are 41.8, 34.7, and 23.7 wt%, respectively (Figure S7).

nodes.characterization_summary: Lattice fringes: 0.285-0.287 nm for Ni₃S₂ (110),(112) planes, 0.261 nm for Cr₂S₃ (113) plane; Ni₃S₂ and Cr₂S₃ in segregated but partially jointed NPs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The unveiled lattice fringes with interplanar spacings of 0.285 and 0.287 nm for Ni₃S₂ and 0.261 nm for Cr₂S₃ can be assigned to the (110) and (112) planes of Ni₃S₂ and the (113) plane of Cr₂S₃. Importantly, it discloses that Ni₃S₂ and Cr₂S₃ are presented in two segregated but partially jointed NPs.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cr K-edge XANES reveals Cr³⁺ valence state in Ni₃S₂/Cr₂S₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cr K-edge XANES spectra of Ni₃S₂/Cr₂S₃ and reference samples (Figure 1f) reveal a 3+ valence state of Cr in Ni₃S₂/Cr₂S₃.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cr K-edge EXAFS shows Cr-O (~1.55 Å) and Cr-S (2.59 Å) bonds.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The presence of peaks at ∼1.55 and 2.59 Å (without phase correction, unless stated) in the Fourier-transformed k³-weighted EXAFS spectrum of Ni₃S₂/Cr₂S₃ (Figure 1g) unveils the presence of Cr-O and Cr-S bonds.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES confirms Ni valence state lower than 2+.
nodes.evidence_snippet: a valence state lower than 2+ for Ni... can be confirmed by the Ni K-edge XANES (Figure 1h)

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge EXAFS shows Ni-O (1.61 Å) and Ni-S (1.97 Å) bonds.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the presence of Ni-O and Ni-S bonds (1.61 and 1.97 Å) in Ni₃S₂/Cr₂S₃ can be confirmed by... Fourier-transformed k³-weighted EXAFS spectra (Figure 1i)

nodes.characterization_summary: Characteristic peaks at 475 and 965 cm⁻¹ assignable to A_g modes of Ni-S vibration, 1440 cm⁻¹ to H-OH bending mode verifying Ni-S bonds and chemically adsorbed water.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The characteristic peaks of 475 and 965 cm⁻¹ shown by the Raman spectrum of Ni₃S₂/Cr₂S₃@NF (Figure S9) are assignable to A_g modes of Ni-S vibration,[33] while the peak at 1440 cm⁻¹ can be attributed to the H-OH bending mode,[34] verifying the presence of Ni-S bonds and chemically adsorbed water molecules.

The peaks at 576.8 and 586.3 eV unveiled by the high-resolution Cr 2p spectrum (Figure S10b) can be associated to Cr³⁺. The Ni 2p spectrum (Figure S10c) can be fitted with one spin-orbit doublet at 855.7 and 873.8 eV ascribable to Ni-O species... the peak centered at 852.3 eV is assignable to the Ni-S bond... The S 2p XPS spectrum (Figure S10e) can be fitted into three peaks, for which the binding energies at 161.5 and 162.7 eV are assignable to S²⁻ 2p₃/₂ and S²⁻ 2p₁/₂... while the peak at 168.6 eV is assignable to SO₄²⁻.

nodes.characterization_summary: Under OCP: Cr³⁺ valence state; under -0.05 V vs RHE: slightly increased Cr valence state due to strong OH⁻/H₂O adsorption on Cr sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It confirms that the valence state of Cr in Ni₃S₂/Cr₂S₃ under the OCP conditions is Cr³⁺, while a slightly increased absorption edge energy from the sample under -0.05 V indicates a slightly increased Cr valence state.

nodes.characterization_summary: Under -0.05 V vs RHE: increased Cr-O peak intensity compared to OCP, indicating increased Cr-O content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: compared to the OCP conditions, the increased Cr-O peak intensity observed under -0.05 V indicates an increased Cr-O content.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni²⁺ valence state unchanged under OCP and -0.05 V vs RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: confirming the presence of Ni²⁺ in all of the Ni₃S₂/Cr₂S₃ samples. The almost identical absorption edge energy from the samples without and with -0.05 V applied potential indicates an almost unchanged Ni valence state.

nodes.characterization_summary: Negligible change in first-shell Ni-O (1.61 Å) intensity under -0.05 V vs RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: only a negligible change for the first-shell Ni-O (1.61 Å, Figure 3d) intensity is observed from Ni₃S₂/Cr₂S₃ under -0.05 V.

nodes.characterization_summary: Under -0.02 V: new peaks at 445 (O-Crᴵᴵᴵ-O), 1395 (Crᴵᴵᴵ-O-H), 1630 cm⁻¹ (H-OH); increasing intensities with potential confirm strong OH⁻/H₂O adsorption on Cr sites; Ni-O at 468 cm⁻¹ from -0.08 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Under a -0.02 V applied voltage, all Raman spectrum peaks of the as-synthesized Ni₃S₂/Cr₂S₃@NF vanished, while three new Raman peaks at 445, 1395, and 1630 cm⁻¹ appeared... As the applied voltage increased, the peak intensities of 445 and 1395 cm⁻¹ are increased... The peak at 468 cm⁻¹ attributing to the Ni-O vibration appears at a -0.08 V applied voltage.
